title: L-tryptophan supplementation decreases cannibalism by megalopae of the Chinese mitten crab, Eriocheir sinensis H. Milne Edwards, 1853 (Decapoda: Brachyura: Varunidae), on stage-5 zoeae in culture
content:
Abstract
Cannibalism by the larvae of the Chinese mitten crab (Eriocheir sinensis H. Milne Edwards, 1853) has seriously hindered the economic benefits of crab farmers. We investigated the effects of L-tryptophan (L-Trp) nutrition regulation on serotonin (5-HT), digestive physiology, and cannibalism of zoea stage 5 (Z5) by the megalopa (M) of E. sinensis. Different gradient concentrations of L-Trp were used to soak the live bait Artemia nauplius (AN) for feeding the Z5 and M. The cannibalism of Z5 by M was observed, and the rate of cannibalism was quantified. The results showed that L-Trp supplementation significantly reduced the frequency of cannibalism (P < 0.05). Physiological and biochemical analysis showed that after feeding AN for 12 h, the activities of the enzymes trypsyn and lypase were significantly increased by L-Trp supplementation; the highest amylase activity was observed in Diet 2 (P < 0.05). After feeding AN for 12 h, the 5-HT level in M was significantly lower in Diet 2 than in Diet 1, whereas significantly higher levels were observed in Diet 3 and Diet 4 (P < 0.05). Compared with Diet 1, the mRNA expression levels of 5-HT1BR and 5-HT7R were significantly upregulated in Diet 2 (P < 0.05). After 24 h of feeding, the 5-HT level in M was significantly higher in Diet 2 and significantly lower in Diet 4 than in Diet 1 (P < 0.05), whereas the mRNA expression levels of 5-HT1BR, 5-HT2BR, and 5-HT7R were significantly downregulated in all L-Trp-supplemented groups (P < 0.05). L-Trp supplementation reduced cannibalism of M on Z5 larvae within the 24 h experimental period and altered digestive enzyme activities, whole-body 5-HT levels, and the expression of 5-HT receptor-related genes in M. The study provides a reference for the healthy breeding of E. sinensis larvae.
